decisions.reason: Restricting filler-image placement to pages with huge empty spaces does not change the approved Inter typeface, font weight, or readability constraint.
The filler-image placement restriction does not alter author names, photos, sizing, sourcing, coverage, or attribution placement.
The source decision concerns filler images used for whitespace and leaves article category labels and their presentation unchanged.
The general obligation to compile supplied materials according to the latest Flat Plan remains valid; the narrower filler-image rule is already owned by the source Requirement.
Limiting where filler images are inserted does not change the polished, modern, brand-aligned visual-style requirement.
The source decision changes filler-image placement, not the requirement to remediate low-quality article images when necessary.
The filler-image placement rule has no effect on the restriction reserving red for the cover.
The decision about filler images does not change which cover-listed articles must be included or who selects their placement.
The supplied tribute page remains required near the end of the magazine and is unrelated to filler images on article pages with huge empty spaces.
Restricting filler-image placement does not change the specified website as the source for article content.
The digital flipbook deliverable remains required unchanged; the source decision only governs filler-image placement within affected article pages.
The current-issue filler-image placement restriction does not alter the separate guidance requirement for future-issue article word counts.
